newsitem.title: USA: United Technologies posts 18 percent income gain.
newsitem.headline: United Technologies posts 18 percent income gain.

text.p: United Technologies Corp., a diversified manufacturer whose products range from air conditioners to helicopters, Wednesday posted a surprisingly strong 18 percent increase in first-quarter profits.

United Technologies said it earned $224 million, or 86 cents a share, on sales of $5.9 billion in the quarter ended March 31. A year earlier it earned $164 million, or 62 cents a share, on sales of $5.4 billion.
Wall Street analysts polled by First Call had expected earnings of 80 cents a share.
The company said foreign currency translation reduced 1997 revenue by $138 million and earnings per share by 3 cents.

The company's Pratt and Whitney unit, which makes and services aircraft engines, posted a 21 percent increase in sales and a 30 percent rise in profits. Continued productivity improvements, higher aftermarket sales, and increased military and commercial engine shipments were partially offset by higher spending on research and development, it said.
One analyst said United Technologies was on track to "slightly exceed" previous growth expectations.
Nick Heymann, analyst at NatWest Securities, said he was raising his 1997 earnings expectations to $4.05 a share from $4.00. For 1998, he upgraded his forecast by 10 cents to $4.70.
"Definitely there's a lot of strength in Pratt that's going to stay," Heymann said.

"Pratt is going to continue, through aggressive cost reduction and through participating in the ramp-up in the (commercial airline) cycle, to see pretty meaningful growth this year, and probably a fair amount of growth next year."
However, Heymann said he was concerned about the company's outlook in its automotive operation, for which sales and operating profit were down in the first quarter.

"In auto, you've got an internal headache with pricing, you have significant problems with the interiors side of the business... (but) that is being reworked. They've brought in a new manager, and I assume we'll see some restructuring."
Heymann lowered his expectations in automotive. "It's going to take a while to fix... We think its operating profit will be down 15 percent over the year. Sales will be down six or seven percent."

United Technologies said its flight systems unit, which includes Sikorsky helicopters and Hamilton Standard, a maker of electronic controls, posted a 41 percent increase in operating profit and an 18 percent rise in sales.

Operating profit at its Otis elevator unit grew 12 percent primarily due to improvement in Europe and the Americas. This was largely offset by the unfavorable impact of foreign currency translation. Sales at the Otis unit rose 5 percent.
Its Carrier unit, which makes heating and air conditioning equipment, posted a 27 percent increase in operating profit and a 5 percent growth in sales.

The Hartford, Conn.-based company also said it revised accounting procedures for international subsidiaries, and if the change had been in effect a year ago, it would have posted earnings of 72 cents a share for the first quarter of 1996.
